idiom_name: try? with ?? (or do/catch + Result), degraded state modelled in the view model
implementation_notes: Swift's error handling composes with the value system: try? turns a throwing call into an optional, ?? (or if-let) supplies the substitute, and do/catch or Result carries a typed failure when the reason matters. Because a throw costs about a return - the language does not unwind the stack - the degraded branch is cheap enough to place at the boundary that owns the policy, and the UI layer models the outcome as an enum (loading/full/degraded) so the degradation is visible. Task cancellation plus a timeout wrapper bound the primary attempt.
pitfalls: try? discards the error entirely: record it before substituting or the degraded path is undiagnosable.
try! or force-unwrapping in the fallback crashes exactly when the system is already unhealthy.
A cached substitute loaded off the main actor must be a Sendable value - passing a reference type across actors after a timeout is a data race.
